London, 24<sup>th</sup> March 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**General Motors of Canada** will save nearly C$1 billion ($819.1 million) on future labor costs as a result of union concessions in March.  The deal with the Canadian Auto Workers union also closes the “per hour” active worker cost gap to the company’s non-union competition in the United States. The deal is contingent upon the company receiving emergency loans from the Canadian government and the province of Ontario.  Company’s executives have taken a 10%salary cut. There will be no bonuses, and all salaried employees are taking big cuts in benefits.  Under the company’s restructuring plan, it would sustain 17 to 20% of its North American production in Canada. 

_Source:  Automotive News_ 

**Japan’s vehicle sales** may fall to the lowest since 1977’s sales of 4.23 million units as the country’s deepening recession discourages customers from visiting showrooms.  Sales of minicars, cars, trucks and buses, may fall 8% to 4.3 million vehicles for the year starting April 1 from estimated 4.67 million this fiscal year, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association (JAMA) said.   Japan’s economy shrank an annualized 12.1% last quarter.   Japanese carmakers are counting on the government’s plan to offer tax breaks on compact cars and other fuel-efficient models from April.   Vehicle sales excluding minicars may fall 9.7% to 2.58 million units next fiscal year. Sales of minicars may fall 5.3% to 1.72 million units. Consumer spending fell 0.4 % last quarter from the previous three months, compared with a record 13.8% decline in exports. The  Tokyo Motor Show will be cut by four days this year. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**LCD panel makers** are concerned about the industry’s outlook for May, as their order visibility has only extended to April, with downstream monitor clients having almost completed their inventory build-up. They are worried that orders will drop sharply in May, traditionally a low month, despite some predictions that rush orders would last until June. Shipments in May-June are expected to drop, but will recover in July-August.  LCD component suppliers also have order visibility extending only as far as April. _Source:  Digitimes_ 

**Sylvania Resources** has successfully commissioned its Lannex tailings dump classification section and PGMs recovery plan in the eastern Bushveld.  The plant is currently in the ramp-up phase, and is forecast to produce at steady state levels of about 2 100 PGMs oz/m by the end of June.  At full production, some 25koz/y will more than double the group’s existing output. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Platmin,** in which Pallinghurst has a 62 % shareholding, hopes to do an inward listing on South Africa’s JSE towards mid-2009.  Platmin CEO Ian Watson said that it had raised $175-million through its arrangement with Pallinghurst and intended extending its bridging finance into a long-term facility, which gave it fully-funded status. Its BE

E partner, the Moepi group, had repaid its $15-million loan.  “So we’re funded to production,” Watson added.  He also said that the company was close to turning its westernlimb Pilanesberg platinum project to account, with milling and concentrate production scheduled to begin this month, and was on track to produce at a rate of 250koz a year. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Lonmin Plc** confirmed Roger Phillimore as chairman after he held the post on an interim basis, the firm said yesterday.  Phillimore, 59, agreed to be interim chairman after John Craven retired on Jan. 29. On Feb. 24, Lonmin said it planned to dismiss up to 5,500 workers at its South African operations after demand tumbled.   Lonmin, whose biggest shareholder is mining group Xstrata with 25%, rejoined the FTSE 100 index on Monday in the latest quarterly reshuffle. _Source:  Mining Weekly_
